title: smart-routing-fallback-cost-draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft to quantify economics and SLO tradeoffs for smart routing policies. Focus: fallback tiers, region routing, and spot vs on-demand instance mixes. Goal is a reproducible cost-per-token model and a set of conservative policy recommendations for Default, Cost-Saver, and High-Availability routing profiles.

Summary (TL;DR):
- We can save ~18–35% unit cost by allowing spot GPUs in non-critical tiers and routing <30% of traffic to secondary regions during normal operation.
- Latency penalty (region hop + cold-spot interruption) needs to be budgeted: assume +10–80 ms median for intra-region spot fallback, +30–200 ms for cross-region fallbacks depending on region pair (US->EU).
- Recommended default policy: primary-on-demand (70%), primary-spot warm pool (20%), secondary-region spot (10%) with conservative timeout/early-fallback thresholds and aggressive caching/prefix reuse applied to cost-tiered traffic.

Assumptions and baseline metrics (spreadsheet-style lines):
- Workload: mix = 60% chat (avg 220 tokens request + 430 tokens response), 40% embedding/ranking (avg 64 tokens).
- Avg tokens per request = 400. Requests/second (RPS) baseline = 120 rps (burst to 500 rps).
- Throughput per GPU (quantized): 1x A100-80GB on-demand = 6k tokens/s sustained for generation workloads; spot instance performance assumed equivalent when running (excl. preemption effects).

Cost inputs (example numbers for modeling):
- On-demand GPU hour (US-west): $3.20/hr (per GPU)
- Spot GPU hour (US-west): $1.05/hr (per GPU)
- On-demand GPU hour (EU-west): $3.60/hr
- Spot GPU hour (EU-west): $1.20/hr
- Average preemption rate (spot): 0.5% per hour (empirical in recent 6-week window)
- Region egress cost for cross-region requests: $0.02 per GB (~0.00002 per token for typical payloads)

Derived unit costs (worked example):
- Tokens/hour per GPU = 6,000 tok/s * 3600 s = 21.6M tokens/hr
- Cost per 1M tokens (on-demand US-west) = (3.20 / 21.6) * 1M = $0.148 per 1M tokens
- Cost per 1M tokens (spot US-west) = (1.05 / 21.6) * 1M = $0.0486 per 1M tokens
- Cross-region egress add-on approx = $0.005 per 1M tokens (negligible at typical sizes but grows with embedding-heavy workloads)

Sample scenario A (Default mix):
- Traffic split: 70% primary on-demand, 20% primary spot warm pool, 10% secondary-region spot.
- Weighted cost per 1M tokens = 0.7*0.148 + 0.2*0.0486 + 0.1*(0.0486 + 0.005) = $0.1163 per 1M tokens (~21.5% savings vs 100% on-demand).

Scenario B (Cost-saver aggressive):
- 40% on-demand, 50% primary spot, 10% secondary spot => weighted cost = 0.4*0.148 + 0.5*0.0486 + 0.1*(0.0486 + 0.005) = $0.0857 per 1M tokens (~42% savings).

Latency and availability adjustments (penalty modeling):
- On-demand primary: baseline median latency = 75 ms for short-turn chat tokens, p95 = 210 ms.
- Primary spot (warm): median +10–30 ms on average due to queuing and instance churn; p95 +40–150 ms depending on pool stability.
- Secondary-region spot: median +40–120 ms (cross-region RTT) and extra p95 tail.
- Preemption modeling: for spot, model a 0.5%/hr preemption. When preemption occurs, requests in flight may restart on fallback path incurring extra cost = extra tokens rerun + double request handling. We model 1% extra token cost per preemption event payload.

Effective SLO impact estimator (map to 99th token latency budget):
- If we accept up to +100 ms added p95 in default profile, we can adopt Scenario A safely for most interactive use-cases. If customer p95 latency SLO < 150 ms, reduce spot fraction to <=10%.

Routing policy primitives (draft pseudo-config):
- route_policy: {    name: "default-cost-aware",    allowed_regions: ["us-west-2", "us-east-1"],    primary_instance_type: ["on-demand-a100"],    fallback_tiers: [      {tier: "primary_spot", fraction: 0.20, max_latency_ms: 80, preempt_handling: "graceful-retry"},      {tier: "secondary_spot", fraction: 0.10, max_latency_ms: 200, region_penalty_ms: 40}    ],    cache_policy: {prefix_kv: true, ttl_seconds: 90} }
Note: above is pseudo-config — real config lives in github repo routing-configs. Need to add unit tests for simulated preemption.

Operational mitigations to reduce risk and effective cost: (implementation side)
- Warm pools with pre-warmed checkpoints and KV cache replication across pools to reduce cold start/cold-KV cost when bouncing to spot nodes.
- Early-detection: track spot preemption heartbeats and proactively redispatch at 80% CPU/latency threshold rather than after failure.
- Request-level hedging for critical requests: replicate to on-demand after 60 ms timeout if not started (configurable per route). Only apply hedging to <5% of traffic to bound extra cost.
- Aggressive prefix caching: apply tighter TTL for chat sessions that are highly repetitive (RLHF/hallucination detection).

Model sensitivity table (quick):
- If spot price increases 30%, cost-saver savings shrink from 42% -> ~36%.
- If preemption increases to 2%/hr, expected extra token reruns and failover cost raises effective spot cost by ~8–12% relative, recommend reducing spot fraction by 10 pts.
- Cross-region egress spikes (x3) move secondary-region routing usefulness to only very cheap workloads (embeddings/batches).

Open questions & TODOs (short list):
- Validate actual per-token throughput on T4/RTX6000 quantized models (we used A100; need lower-bound numbers for smaller instance types). Owner: Diego.
- Backtest with real request traces for 4 representative customers (chat-first consumer app, search-heavy enterprise, embedding-batch pipeline, high-availability fintech). Owner: Mei.
- Add simulation harness to routing-configs repo to iterate on preemption curves and hedging cost tradeoffs. Owner: Ravi.

Draft recommendations (for product and operations):
1) Ship Default profile as Scenario A with conservative timeouts and cache enabled. Track cost delta weekly and surface to customers via console.
2) Offer Cost-Saver profile behind feature flag for self-serve customers who accept p95 > 200 ms. Expose expected monthly cost savings estimate in console before enabling.
3) Add Automatic Safety Net: if observed p95 > configured threshold for >10 min, snapshot policy and temporarily divert >30% of spot traffic to on-demand until stability returns.
4) Implement a per-route hedging toggle (percent and timeout) and monitor incremental token cost via instrumentation.

Notes-to-self: include a small spreadsheet with the formulas used in this doc (columns: region, instance_type, price/hr, tok/s, tok/hr, cost per 1M tok) and upload to the drive folder. Link to policy PR #57 needs tests.

References and quick links:
- cost assumptions doc (internal pricing bucket): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/FIN/Instance+Pricing+2024
- routing config PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-configs/pull/57
- incident log: slack thread #inc-spot-preempt-2024-11 (see OPT-301)

End of draft.

-- Asha
